angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 336,023 km at 22.44 pc = 0.2 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 44.5583 +/- 0.0157 mas (same row, RUWE 1.01): 22.44 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.483 +/- 0.025 solar radii from Brady et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1450 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168...67B/abstract): 336,023 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.48 +/- 0.024 solar masses from Brady et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1450 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168...67B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3437 +/- 86 K from Brady et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1450 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168...67B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Brady et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1450 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168...67B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1450-a.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.751, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
